### Potential Benefits & Traditional Uses

- **Liver & Digestive Support:** Dandelion root acts as a traditional "bitter," which can stimulate digestive enzymes, support bile production in the liver and gallbladder, and help reduce post-meal bloating.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXwQnkf4bxl0c20hCGLIDByBxRbZXHEBUkIZi6eb7I4DggL-gI5ke8FxzGl6iYt6RRaMKpa-icfORxUWFGN0z7rIkBgfz5arb8N7AZKGXnzqYPyL92_2kQKpKte9KwRqO5SITFhhalpajm)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXKajkljLRCF0G1D6_vDy36ZfrNkfBXm0GErsxeH6_b1ZiIbvMh4bu0_84hhovR7zrcJ4KyOgDHqhpMvI6EglAgw-Q2ViMCL-kOM7pY-YX6C0bTX8FCMLG0St2KKbgeqprZqDVpIhcCCtk)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXUG8O1ENZ3vt7q_iYKx5FSgx2crNRv-Q78xfJln2ZhaF5k-OwZlXp9ucK73fk9B2nEnyvhCrpJAriky7ZRxVBzDCgE6TnpMD69it3wKAlbYdoMAx2ecnyqhxDVYG-Ff4vYGxOZD_XDkc)
- **Mild Diuretic Action:** The root and leaves have a mild diuretic effect, helping promote urination and fluid clearance, though most human clinical evidence remains limited.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXZOyv5XXWDxOj_bRU1quZbFECXK0Lfw-GVmniA_CmhHs6v7m0He4NRz5UdrGuInFOKDeXdWVLLWc_BDvRiI0Zs7iECBiQ8SENRC_H7DU3V79HyzJPintjZS_wIxARz9T3VQr0qHUWTuil47LQvsGk)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiwEBxCJF1-bjqcZZBSw6dyZWCDK47_-TXSDxCfLDp8Hs3ypOaUbh0Vnna7xzRqktRTg6OhgxzfBgOl-n8uxrYzdryFve2Kcbwxsuc3qtsow5EYIkOReEB1Z_CqiEX9NJr7cSOYkjG-NSGJ4HCVwcJbavqUgUNyAb3zIq4vpmfpLgutPpAVNH-qCboHrJ)
- **Nutrient & Prebiotic Content:** Dandelion is rich in vitamins (A, C, K) and minerals (calcium, iron, potassium), and the root contains inulin, a prebiotic fiber that feeds beneficial gut bacteria.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXKajkljLRCF0G1D6_vDy36ZfrNkfBXm0GErsxeH6_b1ZiIbvMh4bu0_84hhovR7zrcJ4KyOgDHqhpMvI6EglAgw-Q2ViMCL-kOM7pY-YX6C0bTX8FCMLG0St2KKbgeqprZqDVpIhcCCtk)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESzgEBxCJF1wP3ALDiU1-h9BIEcbjLcDCxfEcyB_vrYb5h44CAVmtYOYjeRj81UQwxRrNgA8mgz0-3Plf-qy2TS52qPDPKUBRgMP2XlyHvzeGJ1KNWKT-nRu7UA2wJ_ZdxgRFrO1eM0q3811GgS6YkwWdaE_yWF_COqLOpJRY5qUgzSk66YSsdZoZllsZZyUuRG3y9cmUBeCTTsinJ2ijLCYvNZ4rUo2e7fzri54Z2Fsd1bgtEWNRaDh0dGswk08t0UZtWEWQkpDXa_kChX07M8A)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZwHEIkXXFl7qBKOwsZcJhWYAQbxsCqAPiAXyCJAjpLw5XMO_bLUPtkX7pWKg6nZK2JWi3-q-qRSdEFA2aKRe3wdqpRDgaBRngvxFd4DyMA_AZ2yp6pHWKsOh926BrnkJZrc7DpOJyEc)

Mild Diuretic Action: The root and leaves have a mild diuretic effect, helping promote urination and fluid clearance, though most human clinical evidence remains limited. Nutrient & Prebiotic Content: Dandelion is rich in vitamins (A, C, K) and minerals (calcium, iron, potassium), and the root contains inulin, a prebiotic fiber that feeds beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Risks, Side Effects & Interactions
items.text: Side Effects: Generally mild, but can include heartburn, mouth sores, upset stomach, or diarrhea. Excessive intake may cause oxalate buildup, increasing the risk of kidney stones. Allergies: Avoid dandelion if you are allergic to plants in the Asteraceae family (such as ragweed, chrysanthemums, marigolds, or daisies). Medication Interactions: Dandelion can interact with diuretics (like Lasix), lithium, and certain diabetes or blood-thinning medications. Pregnancy & Breastfeeding: It is generally recommended to avoid dandelion supplements during pregnancy or nursing due to a lack of safety data. Always consult your healthcare provider before starting any new herbal supplement.
